deep.reconstruction:
LEFT COLUMN (§7 Subtraktion, page numbered 14). This continues §6 (Addition) of the draft of 'Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen'. Let alpha, beta be real numbers given by cuts (A1,A2), (B1,B2) of Q. Put a rational z into C1 if there exist a1 in A1 and b2 in B2 with a1 - b2 >= z; otherwise put z into C2.
(i) Both classes are nonempty. If a1' < a1 and b2' > b2, then a1' - b2' < a1 - b2, so a1' - b2' lies in C1. Every a2 - b1 lies in C2, since a1 < a2 and b1 < b2 give a1 - b2 < a2 - b1 for all choices.
(ii) Every c2 is greater than every c1. If c2 <= c1 <= a1 - b2, then c2 would belong to C1.
(iii) Hence (C1,C2) is a cut. The number gamma it produces is called the difference, gamma = alpha - beta. The note 'auch der Fall, wenn alpha und beta rational sind' (squeezed into the middle column) says this agrees with the old difference for rational alpha, beta. Theorems to be added: (alpha - beta) + beta = alpha, etc.

MIDDLE COLUMN (scratch work: irrationality of the n-th root of a non-n-th-power D, generalising the sqrt(D) argument of 1872, §6).
Setup:
- Let lambda be the integer with lambda^n < D < (lambda+1)^n.
- Suppose t^n = D u^n with positive integers t, u.
- Multiplying by D^{n-1} gives D^{n-1} t^n = (Du)^n.
- Then lambda u < t < (lambda+1) u, so u' = t - lambda u satisfies 0 < u' < u. This is the candidate smaller denominator for a descent.
- Put omega^n = D.
Search for an integral multiplier that makes (t + u omega) times a polynomial in omega linear in omega:
- (t+u omega)(a + a1 omega + ... + a_{n-1} omega^{n-1}) = a t + (a1 t + a u) omega + sum_{k=2}^{n-1} (a_k t + a_{k-1} u) omega^k + D a_{n-1} u.
- Kill the coefficients of omega^2, ..., omega^{n-1}: a_{k+1} t + a_k u = 0. Hence a_{k+1}/a_k = -u/t and a_k = a1 (-u/t)^{k-1}, as written up to a_{n-1}/a1 = (-u/t)^{n-2}.
- Summing the geometric series: the bracket is a + a1 omega (1 - (-u omega/t)^{n-1})/(1 + u omega/t).
- Multiplying by t + u omega = t(1 + u omega/t) gives a(t+u omega) + t a1 omega - t a1 (-u/t)^{n-1} omega^n, with omega^n = D.
- Choosing a1 = b t^{n-2} to clear denominators gives the identity (t+u omega) * P(omega) = a(t+u omega) + b t^{n-1} omega - b(-u)^{n-1} D.

RIGHT COLUMN.
Crossed-out heading, perhaps '§8' / 'Nachtrag'. Then a draft of the sentence that appears, almost verbatim, in the 1872 preface about Cantor's real number magnitudes 'of higher kind': what use the conceptual distinction of such magnitudes could have, Dedekind cannot see, given his conception of the real number domain as complete in itself.
The computation is redone with t - u omega, so that omega = t/u is the hypothetical rational root:
- a(t - u omega) + b(t^{n-1} omega - D u^{n-1}) = (a t - b D u^{n-1}) + (b t^{n-1} - a u) omega.
- Under omega = t/u both brackets t - u omega and t^{n-1} omega - D u^{n-1} vanish, so the sum is 0.
- With a = lambda t^{n-2}, b = 1 [my reading of intent]: lambda t^{n-1} - D u^{n-1} + t^{n-2}(t - lambda u) omega = 0.
- So omega = (D u^{n-1} - lambda t^{n-1}) / (t^{n-2} u'). For n = 2 this is exactly the 1872 descent omega = (Du - lambda t)/(t - lambda u). For n > 2 the denominator t^{n-2} u' is not smaller than u, so the descent does not close.
Dedekind then tries the direct route:
- D(t - lambda u)^n = omega^n u^n (omega - lambda)^n = (omega^2 - lambda omega)^n u^n = (omega t - lambda u omega)^n = (t omega - lambda t)^n = (t^2/u - lambda t)^n.
- That is, D u'^n = (t u'/u)^n, with t' = omega u' = t u'/u.
- For the descent one needs t' to be an integer. For n = 2 it is (t' = Du - lambda t), but in general this is not shown. The page breaks off here.

[My remark:] the descent can be repaired by taking u minimal with u omega^k in Z for k = 0..n-1. Then u(omega - lambda) has the same property, which is the module/ideal form of the argument.
errors: §7: the proof that C2 > C1 writes 'aus c1 < a1 - b2', copied from the addition proof. Under the stated definition (a1 - b2 >= z) it should read c1 <= a1 - b2. The argument is unaffected.
Middle column: in the first bracket the second term is written as -(u/t) omega. It should be -(u omega/t) omega, i.e. a1 omega * (-u omega/t); the following lines use the correct geometric series.

Right column: the n-th-root descent is not completed. The new numerator t' = t u'/u (equivalently (D u^{n-1} - lambda t^{n-1})/t^{n-2}) is not shown to be an integer, and the denominator t^{n-2} u' is not smaller than u. The method only works as written for n = 2. This is an incomplete attempt rather than a false claim.
Minor: 'b t^n omega' in some readings should be b t^{n-1} omega; the image supports t^{n-1}.

results.what: Definition of the difference alpha - beta of two cuts: z in C1 iff z <= a1 - b2 for some a1 in A1, b2 in B2; proof that this is a cut
results.usually_credited_to: Dedekind 1872 (Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen, §6, which treats only addition in detail and says the other operations are analogous)

results.what: Attempt to generalise the 1872 descent proof of irrationality of sqrt(D) to n-th roots of a non-n-th-power D, via multipliers in Z[omega] that reduce (t +/- u omega)P(omega) to a linear form in omega
results.modern_name: Irrationality of D^(1/n) for D not a perfect n-th power (descent / denominator-ideal argument; integrally closed Z)
results.usually_credited_to: Classical (Euclid X for squares; general case folklore, e.g. Gauss's lemma / rational root theorem)

results.what: Draft of the remark on the uselessness of Cantor's 'real number magnitudes of higher kind'
results.modern_name: Dedekind's comment on Cantor 1872 in the preface of Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a working draft for Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen. It contains subtraction of cuts (routine, analogous to the published addition) and a draft of a known sentence from the 1872 preface. It also has an unfinished attempt to extend the sqrt(D) descent to n-th roots, using multipliers from Z[omega] that foreshadow module-theoretic thinking. This is a mildly interesting unpublished detail, but neither new nor completed.

With a1 = b t^{n-2}, the term t a1(-u/t)^{n-1} equals b(-u)^{n-1}.

checkable.asserts: If w = t/u is a rational n-th root of D, the right-column expression vanishes identically.
D(t - lambda u)^n = (t^2/u - lambda t)^n when t^n = D u^n.
The n=2 descent identity: t^2 = D u^2 implies (Du - lambda t)^2 = D(t - lambda u)^2, which is the 1872 sqrt(D) proof the page tries to generalise.
From t^n = D u^n follows D^{n-1} t^n = (Du)^n.

transcription_corrections: The right-column prose is a draft of the 1872 preface sentence. It reads approximately: 'Welchen Nutzen aber die, wenn auch nur begriffliche, Unterscheidung von reellen Zahlgrößen noch höherer Art gewähren kann [sollte], vermag ich gerade nach meiner Auffassung des reellen Zahlgebietes als eines in sich vollkommenen (noch) nicht zu erkennen'. 'die ich für vollkommener' and 'Zahlgebiete' are misreadings.
The line '$\frac{D}{\omega^n} = 1 \ldots$' and the heading 'Abschnitt[?]' are doubtful. The right column has a small '§8' (or similar) above a crossed-out heading, not a formula.
'auch der Fall, wenn alpha und beta rational sind' belongs to §7 (subtraction agrees with the old difference for rationals), not to the middle-column computation.
In the first bracketed expression the second term should be read as -(u omega/t) omega (geometric series in -u omega/t), not -(u/t) omega.
In §7 the proof clause should read 'aus c1 <= a1 - b2' given the definition with >=; the manuscript has '<'.
Final middle-column line: a(t+u omega) + b t^{n-1} omega - b(-u)^{n-1} D (exponent n-1 on t).
